question: Secularism is a feature of the Indian Constitution, which means:

options.text: The State promotes the religion of the majority community.
The State does not promote any religion.
The State can promote any religion.
The State promotes the religion of the minority community.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The State does not promote any religion.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Secularism** in the Indian Constitution means that the State does not promote any religion.
 
• This ensures that there is no official state religion and that all religions are treated equally by the state.
 
• It is a fundamental aspect that protects the rights of individuals to practice and propagate their religion without any state interference.
 
• Secularism helps in maintaining the principle of separation of religion from the state, thus ensuring that religious groups do not interfere in government affairs and the government does not interfere in religious affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of **secularism** is enshrined in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution, which declares India to be a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic.
 
• The Constitution guarantees the right to freedom of religion to all its citizens under **Articles 25 to 28**.
 
• Article 25 provides for freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.
 
• Article 26 ensures freedom to manage religious affairs.
 
• Article 27 ensures that no person shall be compelled to pay any taxes for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion.
 
• Article 28 allows educational institutions maintained by the state to impart religious instruction.
